title: What a delegate_task call hands over cannot leave its frame: its task, set apart in `<task>` once a block follows it, cannot close it to fake the runtime's next block, and is read as it is alone; a closing tag what it passed holds is neutralised, as a JSON string would hide it, a text past the bound is cut at a word and marked; a context that is no object still reaches the worker, under `context`, and the task ends as any other; only null and an empty string, list or object are no context
notes: Python: tests/tasks/test_delegate_reach.py; tasks/delegate.py _passed_context, tasks/brief.py context_block, task_brief (the task under `Your task, as the delegating agent wrote it:` in `<task>` once a block follows it, HITL 90c4e28a; a task with no block after it is the worker's whole instruction, read as it is). The bound is on the JSON text, 4000 characters, its cut ending in … as bounded_text writes it. Each string, a key included, at any depth, is read as json_text_line reads a text (a look-alike of a double quote made a single one) and for a tag before it is written as JSON, which would hide a line break or a slash as an escape. A model may send a string where the tool says object: `{**context}` and the task's metadata both read an object, so the handler makes it one. 0 and false are values: only null, an empty string, an empty list and an empty object are no context.
